result.title: Engram Injection: A Study of Temporal Validity in Parametric Language-Model Memory
result.summary: A stored fact may stop being valid when a user changes a preference or an event replaces an earlier one. We study whether a language model can learn these changes in its parameters and answer correctly from only a question and the current time. Engram Injection stores facts in LoRA adapters and supplies the clock through FiLM conditioning on a frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct model. We compare it with additive clock conditioning, prompting with the full dated history, and retrieving four dated records. We train six matched adapters across three seeds after fixing a sampler that could admit test-age examples into training. The training audit reports no such examples among 127,760 evaluated training inputs. On 62 pairs of questions asked before and after an update, at an elapsed age of seven days excluded from training, both adapter methods answer zero pairs correctly under the primary blinded assistant review with order code 1 held fixed. Full-history prompting answers 59/62 pairs correctly, and retrieval answers 62/62. Separate experiments show that adapters can store facts and that removable memory units can support local deletion. Combining fact selection with time-based version selection remains unsuccessful. These results separate learning a fact from learning when to use it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究语言模型能否仅凭问题与当前时间在参数中学会事实的时效变更：用 LoRA 适配器存事实、FiLM 注入时钟，并与带日期全历史提示、检索四条记录对比；结果显示适配器方法在训练未见的七天时点上版本选择全错，而提示与检索几乎全对，据此区分「学到事实」与「学会何时使用」。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心诊断（去掉提示或检索后，参数状态是否真被用于输出）与 LVR 中信息坍缩、视觉旁路及 latent 贡献分配的核查思路相通，「可删除记忆单元」与训练审计也可能供借鉴；但该工作为纯文本设定，迁移到多模态推理状态尚需核查。
